story.lead: Antwan Raymond ran for 140 yards and three touchdowns to lead Rutgers to a 58-7 victory over Howard on Friday night.
paragraphs: Antwan Raymond ran for 140 yards and three touchdowns to lead Rutgers to a 58-7 victory over Howard on Friday night.

story.headline: Lee Beebe Jr. rushes for 203 yards and No. 4 Indiana holds off surprising Northwestern 29-23
story.lead: Indiana running back Lee Beebe Jr. waited a whole year for an opportunity like the one he got Friday night.
paragraphs: Indiana running back Lee Beebe Jr. waited a whole year for an opportunity like the one he got Friday night.
And with starting running back Turbo Richard out with an injury, Beebe gladly showed everyone what he could do.

On a night the Hoosiers looked nothing like the defending national champs, Beebe carried 24 times for 203 yards, scored one touchdown and his late 70-yard burst set up Josh Hoover's game-sealing 1-yard score with 1:56 to go as No. 5 Indiana held on for a 29-23 victory over Northwestern. Beebe was so good, he even earned the highest praise from coach Curt Cignetti.

“That guy’s got a lot of heart,” Cignetti said. “Boy, he’s got as much heart as anyone that’s been in this program the last three years. Not only didn’t he step in, he played and fortunately they couldn’t tackle him. It was all grit and heart.”

story.headline: Bryant Wesco's punt return TD leads Clemson to a 24-10 win over Cal
story.lead: Bryant Wesco Jr. had Clemson's first punt return touchdown in eight years to break a tie late in the third quarter and the Tigers went on to beat California 24-10 Friday night in a game where both offenses struggled.
paragraphs: Bryant Wesco Jr. had Clemson's first punt return touchdown in eight years to break a tie late in the third quarter and the Tigers went on to beat California 24-10 Friday night in a game where both offenses struggled.
Both Clemson (3-1, 2-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) and Cal (2-2, 1-1) struggled to generate much offense in the first matchup between the schools since the Golden Bears joined the ACC in 2024.

The teams combined for one offensive touchdown until Gideon Davidson put the game away with a 75-yard run with 2:59 to play. Davidson finished with 159 yards rushing and two TDs to give the Tigers their third straight win since a lopsided loss in the opener against LSU.

“Two games in a row, we’ve played some complimentary football,” coach Dabo Swinney said. “When we do, it’s a really good thing. But we’re a long way away from hoisting a trophy or anything like that. But at the end of the day, we’re 3-1. We’re still undefeated in the league and just got to keep finding a way to keep growing, learning."

story.headline: Arch Manning visits stadium where Uncle Peyton dominated in Texas' 1st trip to Tennessee
story.lead: Arch Manning finally visits Neyland Stadium where his uncle Peyton made quite the legacy for himself when top-ranked Texas visits No. 14 Tennessee.
paragraphs: Arch Manning finally visits Neyland Stadium where his uncle Peyton made quite the legacy for himself when top-ranked Texas visits No. 14 Tennessee.

Texas coach Steve Sarkisian doesn't want his quarterback trying to live up to anyone else on Saturday. Not grandfather Archie nor either of his championship-winning uncles, Peyton and Eli. Don't compare the current quarterback to Colt McCoy or Vince Young of the Longhorns' past either.
“I want him to be Arch Manning, and Arch Manning is plenty good enough to put us in position to win,” Sarkisian said.

The last time a Manning played at Neyland Stadium, Peyton led the Volunteers to a win over Vanderbilt on Nov. 29, 1997. This time, his nephew leads the Longhorns (3-0) against Tennessee (3-0) in the Southeastern Conference opener for both teams.

story.lead: Ryan Day has more than a couple areas of concern as seventh-ranked Ohio State hosts Illinois to open Big Ten Conference play on Saturday.
paragraphs: Ryan Day has more than a couple areas of concern as seventh-ranked Ohio State hosts Illinois to open Big Ten Conference play on Saturday.
With three important October road tests on the horizon, Day is seeking more balance on offense, better execution in the red zone and on third down.

"I think it’s been inconsistent,” Day about the offense. “There’s been times where it’s been very good and then other times where it’s struggled. I think that the situations in particular, we’ve got stalled because we haven’t been able to finish drives in the red zone.”
The Buckeyes (2-1) are 12 of 17 scoring touchdowns in the red zone but went 2 of 5 in their 24-23 loss at No. 1 Texas on Sept. 12.

story.lead: Eight years ago, Oklahoma and Georgia clashed in a thrilling double-overtime Rose Bowl, one that sent the Bulldogs to face Alabama in the 2018 national championship.
paragraphs: Eight years ago, Oklahoma and Georgia clashed in a thrilling double-overtime Rose Bowl, one that sent the Bulldogs to face Alabama in the 2018 national championship.
The Sooners and Bulldogs haven’t met since. That changes Saturday, when a freshly unranked Oklahoma team heads to Athens to face No. 2 Georgia in what is now a Southeastern Conference matchup.
Oklahoma enters the outing with much to prove, having fallen 17-10 to Michigan in Week 2 and narrowly beaten New Mexico 14-6 the following week after entering the game as a 21.5-point favorite.

Georgia has yet to be challenged, with defensive line coach Tray Scott running drills during television timeouts against Arkansas as tangible proof. The Bulldogs have cruised to a 3-0 record and have a plus-138 scoring differential.

“They are not high-priced talent kids just there playing football, collecting NIL. That’s not at all what they are,” Drinkall said. "The Miami Hurricanes organization is a professional organization ... you could make an argument they’re the most talented team in college football. I could sit and then make an argument that they are more well-coached than they are talented and that their culture is as good as their coaching.”
